chief_complaint: anterior knee ache behind the kneecap worsening when sitting for long periods (theater sign) or climbing stairs in young female athlete
hpi_details: 23F volleyball player presenting with peripatellar ache, positive J-sign/lateral patellar tracking, and positive Clarke grind test without effusion responding to targeted physical therapy strengthening of the Vastus Medialis Obliquus (VMO) and hip external rotators.
ideas: She thinks she wore down the protective cushioning behind her kneecap from repeated hard landings on the volleyball court.
concerns: She is worried that her knee is permanently damaged and that she will be forced to give up playing competitive volleyball before the upcoming tournament.
expectations: She hopes to get an MRI of her knee to check for structural damage and targeted exercises so she can sit through long lectures without aching.

teaching.one_liner: Anterior knee pain arising from the patellofemoral joint, typically aggravated by stairs, running, squatting, or prolonged sitting.
red_flags: Acute hot swollen joint or fever
True locking, traumatic instability, or inability to bear weight

must_ask.say: Is the pain worse with stairs, squatting, running, or sitting with your knee bent for a long time?
Is the pain behind or around the kneecap rather than along the joint line?
Have you recently increased your running, jumping, or other training?
Has the knee become swollen, locked, or given way after an injury?
Have you noticed your kneecap shifting or the knee tracking inward during squats or stairs?

history.answer: My right knee has been aching right behind and around the kneecap, especially when I climb stairs or sit for a long movie.
It is specifically in my right knee, deep around and behind the kneecap. My left knee feels completely normal.
It started gradually about a month ago and has slowly gotten more noticeable over the past couple of weeks.
It is a dull, nagging ache behind the kneecap. After a long practice or climbing several flights of stairs, it gets up to about a 5 out of 10.
No, I haven't noticed any visible swelling, redness, or heat in the knee joint.
I do not have stiffness when I wake up in the morning. It only feels stiff when I've been sitting still with my knees bent for a long time.
Sitting for long periods like at the movies or at my desk, squatting down, and climbing stairs make it worse. Keeping my leg straight and resting helps.
I can walk on flat ground without trouble, but going up and down stairs hurts, and jumping during volleyball practice is getting difficult.
I actually stepped up my jump-training drills and court practice sessions about six weeks ago for our upcoming season.
Sometimes it feels like my kneecap is tracking slightly off-center or catching with a faint grinding sensation when I straighten the leg.
No, there was no direct fall, blow, twisting injury, popping sound, or sensation of the knee giving way or locking up.
No, I have had no fever, chills, or night sweats.
No, this is the very first time I have experienced pain like this in my knee.
No, I haven't felt unusually fatigued, and I haven't had any weight loss or low fevers.
No, I have no skin rashes, no dandruff or scaly patches, no mouth ulcers, and no eye redness or dryness.
No, I do not have any inflammatory lower back pain in the morning, heel pain, or swelling of my fingers or toes.
No recent diarrhea, no burning or discharge when I urinate, and no recent sore throat.
I only have a drink socially once or twice a month, I eat a balanced diet, and I do not take water pills.
No, I have never had any steroid injections, hyaluronic acid injections, or joint surgeries.
I am in a monogamous relationship with my long-term partner, and I have not had any new sexual contacts.
I thought all the jumping and hard landings on the court might have completely worn away the cushion behind my kneecap.
I'm really scared that I ruined my knee for good and won't be cleared to play in our university tournament next month.
I'm hoping to get an MRI to see what's wrong inside, plus some specific exercises so my knee doesn't ache so badly when I sit through class.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or inflammatory arthritis.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I am not taking any regular medications or supplements, just an occasional ibuprofen if the ache flares up after practice.
I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or materials.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco or vaping products.
I am a 23-year-old university student living in a campus apartment, and I play collegiate club volleyball.
No one in my family has rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, gout, or any other autoimmune diseases.
My last menstrual period was two weeks ago, my cycles are regular every 28 days, I'm not pregnant, and we use barrier protection consistently.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 116/74 mmHg, pulse 68 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Well-nourished, athletic young female resting comfortably without acute distress.

Right knee exhibits mild peripatellar tenderness, positive Clarke grind test reproducing retropatellar pain, and lateral patellar tracking with positive J-sign during terminal extension; no joint effusion, warmth, erythema, joint line tenderness, or ligamentous instability.
Normal non-antalgic gait on level ground, with discomfort reproduced during a single-leg squat and simulated stair stepping.
Full 5/5 motor strength in bilateral lower extremities, with noticeable mild fatigue and weakness during isolated right hip external rotation and vastus medialis testing.
No psoriatic plaques, malar rash, tophi, oral ulcers, or nail pitting on skin examination.
